newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Truck strike threatens oil refinery output.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Truck strike threatens oil refinery output.

text.p: France's oil industry prepared to slow down its refineries on Wednesday as a truckers' blockade tightened against companies already struggling to supply petrol.

In another complication, France's largest oil firm Elf Aquitaine said it was forced to close its Grandpuits refinery near Paris for 24 hours on Wednesday because of an unrelated protest by distribution workers.
Oil industry association UFIP said for the first time on Wednesday that a blockade of oil installations had become a threat to production at some of France's 13 oil refineries.
"We are starting to see a slight risk of cuts in production at the refineries, especially in the south," an UFIP spokeswoman told Reuters on the 10th day of the strike.
Truckers have singled out the oil industry for the tightest road blockades designed to put pressure on the government and persuade haulage bosses to negotiate better pay and conditions.
Local government prefects have imposed petrol rationing in some areas, allowing only priority vehicles to refuel.

Drivers and employers made progress on key demands in marathon talks on Wednesday but truckers said some 218 roadblocks that have led to fuel rationing and closed factories in some regions would stay until an overall deal was struck.

An official at France's third largest refinery, operated by oil major Royal Dutch/Shell at Berre, near Marseille, said the plant was getting ready for cuts of between 20 and 30 percent in production from Thursday if the strike continued.
Berre is one of a dozen French refineries which have seen their road deliveries cut off one-by-one by truckers' blockades over the past week.
Refiners have until now been able to maintain their production since only a third of their output usually leaves by road tanker, the rest being transported by pipeline.
The Shell plan to cut output mainly reflects problems in getting deliveries into the plant through the blockade, rather than the lack of storage space for products being distilled.
"We are not getting supplies of chemicals we need to do things like make steam," the Berre refinery official said.
Away from the giant oil complexes, most of France's 175 strategic fuel depots were also surrounded by parked lorries or cars, preventing deliveries.
Oil officials said truckers were running well-organised and flexible blockades at the depots, linked together by radio.
The number of France's 18,000 petrol stations facing temporary closure or shortage rose to 1,000 on Wednesday from barely more than a hundred on Monday, UFIP said.
Most of these were in the south, southwest and northwest of the country. Paris went on as normal even though one of the blocked fuel depots was near the capital, oil executives said.
The disruption at Elf's Grandpuits refinery was carried out by workers at distribution subsidiary Elf Antar. They oppose plans by the firm to shed 10 percent of its staff or 330 people.
Elf and trade union spokesmen said further one-day protests were expected at two other refineries, Elf plants at Donges in western France and Feyzin near Lyon, on Thursday.
Although Elf has had time to prepare for the Antar strikes, the action will be a headache to managers at Feyzin which is the only French refinery not ringed off in the truck dispute.
